name: Moped
description: A motorcycle with pedals for human propulsion and a motor of not more than two brake horsepower (1,492 W) that can't propel it past 30 mph on level ground; an electric motor qualifies, since only a combustion engine is held to 50 cc. Defined by Utah Code §41-6a-102, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026), effective May 6, 2026.
restrictions: Pedals that permit propulsion by human power, and a power drive system that works without clutching or shifting once engaged
Its motor produces not more than two brake horsepower (1,492 W) and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground
Not an electric assisted bicycle or a motor assisted scooter
Counted as a motorcycle under the traffic code since May 6, 2026
Riders need a driver's license but no motorcycle endorsement
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway
Titled and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles
Not allowed on sidewalks or on roads with four or more lanes for regular traffic, and should ride close to the right side of the roadway
